title: Active tandem edge switchover with circuit throttles and stream-preserving handoff
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design and implement an active-active regional switchover pattern for Redwood's hosted API gateway that preserves streaming session continuity where possible, exposes circuit throttle primitives for graceful degradation, and integrates SLO-driven load-shedding policies. This ticket covers design, prototype, tests, and an initial canary rollout for a single customer cohort.
background: Observed risk: cross-region failovers currently cause abrupt stream termination for long-lived connections and token loss for in-flight requests.
Goal: minimize user-visible disruption during region failover while protecting global SLOs and preventing cascading overloads.
Constraints: cannot change existing SDK websocket handshake semantics for GA; must interoperate with KV cache behavior and streaming token preservation logic in the runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic (10% of calls from selected region) can be shifted to secondary region with <= 250ms median additional tail latency for establish-phase requests and <= 2% increase in request error-rate.
Active streaming sessions are preserved across a soft cutover where possible: clients see an uninterrupted stream or a resumable 'stale-offset' handshake enabling continuation within 30s.
Circuit-throttle policy triggers when regional CPU or queue depth breaches defined headroom; when triggered, priority and degrade rules are applied and documented in dashboard.
Runbook updated with step-by-step rollback, forced cutover, and postmortem checklist.
design_decisions: Use 'tandem switchover' flow: new region is brought to warm-ready state, ephemeral proxies perform gradual traffic mirror+diverge, then live weight shift in 5 phased steps.

Streaming: implement per-session checkpointing metadata (opaque resume token) stored in the regional KV cache with TTL and cross-region propagation hooks; prefer in-memory transfer when available to avoid cold rehydration latency.

Circuit throttles: introduce a lightweight token-bucket controller at the gateway ingress with two thresholds: 'soft' where low-priority requests are shed, and 'hard' where all non-critical routes are rejected with 429+Retry-After.

Load-shedding policy: SLO-priority tiers (P0 app traffic, P1 standard, P2 cheap/prompts) map to routing and degradation behaviors. Quantization/approximate responses are an option for P2 during sustained pressure.
Telemetry gate: use combined signal of regional queue depth, 99th tail latency, and runtime headroom to trigger each phase transition, with manual override capability.
implementation_steps: Design API for resume-token exchange and document in console API spec.
Extend regional KV sync prototype to replicate small resume-token entries with bounded staleness semantics.
Add ingress circuit token-bucket controller to the edge proxy; expose thresholds via config and console UI.
Implement phased traffic weight controller: mirror, 5% live traffic, 25% live, 60% live, full cutover. Each step gated by telemetry and delay timers.
Add stream-resume handshake in runtime: on reconnect, client supplies resume-token and desired offset; runtime validates token and replays KV-cached context to restore session.
Create synthetic and chaos test harness for long-lived streaming sessions and token-loss scenarios.
open_questions: How to ensure resume-token confidentiality when stored in KV that may be replicated across regions? Consider encrypting tokens with region-specific KEKs or short TTLs.
What maximum rehydration latency is acceptable for enterprise customers requiring 99.9% streaming continuity? Need sign-off from Solutions team.
Edge case: mobile clients behind NAT with short-lived sockets that cannot re-establish within TTL window — fallback UX needed.
progress_updates: 2026-01-20: Initial design doc reviewed with SRE and Runtime teams; agreed on tandem switchover phases and telemetry gates.
2026-01-28: KV resume-token prototype implemented; simple TTL-based replication validated in staging across two regions.
2026-02-02: Ingress circuit controller PoC added to edge proxy; local unit tests covering soft and hard threshold behavior passing.
2026-02-05: Began integration testing with streaming handshake; observed a median 120ms resume time for warm cache, 1.8s for cold rehydrate.
test_plan: Unit tests for resume-token lifecycle (issue, store, revoke, expire).
Load test: simulate 10k concurrent long-lived streams and perform phased cutover, measure continuity and errors.
Chaos test: force regional CPU spike and validate circuit throttle sheds low-priority traffic while preserving P0 routes.
Canary: 2 customer orgs in staging, shift 10% production-ish traffic for 48 hours and validate SLO metrics.
monitoring_and_alerting: New dashboards: 'Edge Tandem Cutover' showing phase, weight, resume-success-rate, average resume latency, resumed tokens per minute.
Alerts: resume-success-rate < 95% for 5m, regional queue depth > 80% headroom for 3m, circuit throttle firing > 10% of requests for 1m.
Audit logs: every resume token lookup must be logged with caller region and decision (hit/miss/expired).
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal traffic only, single replica in secondary region for 1 week.
Beta: 2 customer orgs, 10% sticky traffic for 48 hours, manual sign-off required to progress.
GA: 100% traffic shift allowed via automated phased controller with telemetry gate enabled.
Rollback: reverse weight in mirroring mode, or immediate cutback to primary region if resumed-failure-rate exceeds threshold.
